---
title: "Phase-Space Volume Element"
source_chapter: "2"
source_section: "2.2.3"
source_page: 65
---

> [!TLDR]
> Phase-space volume combines coordinate and momentum intervals; semiclassical state counting uses one cell of action h per degree of freedom.

The volume element in Γ-space is:

$$
\mathrm d\Gamma=\prod_{i=1}^{3{\mechanical{N}}}\mathrm d{\mechanical{q}}_i\,\mathrm d{\mechanical{p}}_i.
$$

Fig. 2.1 shows trajectories of one particle in one dimension.

**Fig. 2.1** Phase-space trajectories of a one-dimensional harmonic oscillator. Each ellipse has constant energy ${\energy{E}}={\mechanical{p}}^2/(2{\mechanical{m}})+{\mechanical{k}}{\mechanical{q}}^2/2$. The trajectories do not intersect. The shaded annulus is the phase-space volume $\Delta\Gamma$ associated with the energy interval $[{\energy{E}},{\energy{E}}+\Delta {\energy{E}}]$.

> [!note] Elementary phase-space cells
> The Heisenberg relation $\Delta {\mechanical{q}}_i\Delta {\mechanical{p}}_i\geq{\energy{\hbar}}/2$ motivates a finite resolution in phase space. The state-counting measure ${\energy{h}}=2\pi{\energy{\hbar}}$ per degree of freedom comes from semiclassical counting, for example Bohr–Sommerfeld quantization or plane waves in a finite periodic volume. It does not follow by setting the uncertainty inequality to equality. For ${\mechanical{N}}$ monatomic particles in three dimensions, the elementary cell has measure ${\energy{h}}^{3{\mechanical{N}}}$. This factor is needed in [[02.05.01 Counting Microstates]].

## Physical quantities

| Symbol | Unit | Quantity | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${\mechanical{q}}$ | $\unit{m}$ | Position coordinate | A Cartesian coordinate; generalized coordinates can have different units. |
| ${\mechanical{p}}$ | $\unit{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$ | Momentum | Momentum conjugate to a Cartesian position coordinate. |
| ${\mechanical{N}}$ | $1$ | Particle or oscillator count | The number of particles or distinguishable oscillators. |
| ${\energy{E}}$ | $\unit{J}$ | Energy | The system or level energy; ΔE is an energy interval. |
| ${\mechanical{m}}$ | $\unit{kg}$ | Mass | The particle or oscillator mass. |
| ${\mechanical{k}}$ | $\unit{N\,m^{-1}}$ | Spring constant | The stiffness in the harmonic potential. |
| ${\energy{h}}$ | $\unit{J\,s}$ | Planck constant | The action scale in semiclassical state counting. |
| ${\energy{\hbar}}$ | $\unit{J\,s}$ | Reduced Planck constant | Planck constant divided by 2π. |
| $\mathrm d\Gamma$ | $\unit{(J\,s)^{3N}}$ | Phase-space volume element | The product of all coordinate and conjugate-momentum intervals in three dimensions. |
